base_sha_note: First phase of the Phase 11B-11E mixed Q8/Q5 chain; base is main's tip at the time ("feat: add adaptive Q8/Q5 KV policy", PR #20) -- the whole-cache adaptive policy this chain compares itself against throughout.
purpose: Determine whether per-layer heterogeneous Q8_0/Q5_1 KV storage (as opposed to the already-shipped whole-cache adaptive Q8-or-Q5 choice) is mechanically feasible using existing MEMBRANE infrastructure (the Phase 4.1 kv_type_override patch), and whether a sensitivity-based layer-selection policy beats naive equal-memory layouts.
verdict_summary: Mixed per-layer Q8_0/Q5_1 KV works mechanically with zero llama.cpp/upstream changes -- it reuses the already-accepted, already-shipped kv_type_override callback unchanged. A sensitivity-based (highest-error-first) layer-selection policy beat every naive layout (early/late/alternating/random) at equal memory on a small 5-prompt sample (best delta_nll, competitive logit_rel_l2, best top1_preservation). Generation throughput across all-Q8/all-Q5/mixed was statistically indistinguishable at this small model's scale (differences within run-to-run noise) -- feasible and mechanically safe, but no throughput advantage demonstrated, and the positive quality result was disclosed as a small, single-model, single-context sample motivating the generalization check in Phase 11C.
verdict_source: results/canonical/mixed-layer-q8-q5-feasibility.json: feasibility_classification, sensitivity_based_policy_vs_naive.note, performance.note (literal source fields, not synthesized)
hardware: Real GTX 1650 (Vulkan backend) for GPU throughput numbers; same host's CPU for CPU throughput numbers
follow_up: This phase's own limitations (5-prompt subset, single model, single context) directly motivated Phase 11C's generalization study (does the sensitivity ranking hold across more prompts, categories, models, and context sizes?). Source HEAD eaeb25fed8c12bf924f5f42a3d78cd151cd130ca.
